I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County that is the crop pattern I trust most, because the land, weather, machinery, and local markets all fit it well, and at my age I want a stable, familiar system rather than something more complicated. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will focus first on topdressing, watering at key stages, and controlling weeds and disease so I can secure a solid wheat harvest. After harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize on the same land, because that double-cropping system makes the best use of the year and gives me the most reliable total output.

I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care most about steady yield and risk control. For wheat, I will give enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, with moderate phosphorus and potassium for roots and lodging resistance. I will irrigate around the jointing, heading, and grain-filling periods if water is available. For maize, I will use one-shot basal fertilizer plus topdressing, keep plant population even, and rely on fewer irrigations because the summer rains usually help. I will not make the plan too fancy. I will use the tillage method that saves labor and fits the season: rotary tillage for wheat establishment and no-tillage or minimal disturbance after wheat harvest for maize, so I can sow fast and keep moisture.
